_comment: senseFly/AgEagle eBee X mapping drone, in its endurance-battery configuration: the '90 minutes, 95 km' figure.
_inferred:
senseFly does NOT publish battery capacity — the weak point of this example, and the same reason the Wingcopter 198 was rejected as a VTOL example. Wing area, CD0, Oswald, motor and propeller parameters are also unpublished.

What makes it usable anyway: the endurance and the range are published TOGETHER, so they pin the average cruise speed at 95 km / 90 min = 17.6 m/s. Battery energy is then set so the model reaches 90 min AT that speed — and the range falls out as a consequence rather than being fitted. Two published numbers satisfied by one choice is a weaker check than the M300's, but it is not circular.
_calibration:
Battery capacity is the ONE fitted number: 6200 mAh at 4S, chosen so the model reaches the published 90 min at the 17.6 m/s the published range-and-endurance pair implies. The check is what happens next — range comes out at 94.9 km against a published 95, and it was not fitted. Stall lands at 9.1 m/s, below the published 11 m/s bottom of the cruise band, as it must be.

This is weaker evidence than the M300, where the battery is published and nothing at all was tuned. Treat the eBee X as a plausible reconstruction that satisfies every published number, not as manufacturer data.
